messages:
Devon: Alert — auth anomaly detector flagged a wave of session revokes + account lockouts in us-west-2 over the last 12m. Clusters share same user-agent + rapidly rotating source IPs. Could be assertion/cookie replay. Posting quick summary and sample logs.
ops-bot: [automated] Auth-anomaly-detector triggered: 3,712 lockouts, 13,980 MFA prompts, 4,210 session.revoke events. Top src IPs: 54.12.23.45, 18.204.17.92. Incident id: 1978504321
Sara: On it. Pulling auth logs and SAML assertion trace. @Natalie can you pull KMS & CloudTrail for any unusual decrypts or key usage spikes? Need to rule out KMS misuse.
Natalie: Pulling now. Quick glance: no unusual KMS Decrypt calls for customer keys. CloudTrail shows heavy GetSessionToken activity from service account `legacy-integration` starting ~02:14 UTC.
Jamie: Checking recent RBAC/IAM changes and deploys to our SSO connectors. Will grep deploy history and infra PRs.
Devon: Temporary mitigation rolled: increased per-tenant MFA throttle (30/min) for region, lowered SAML assertion validity window from 15m -> 60s for affected pool, and enabled targeted session revocation for sessions originating from suspect IPs. Notifying SOC for customer comms.
Leo: A few customers reporting MFA-push fatigue. Suggest we enable push-suppression (suppress duplicate pushes for 5m) for any tenant with anomalous push volume. Also prepare a short customer note.
Sara: Found repeated successful assertion exchange with same assertion id — looks like replay. Example snippet:
```
saml.assertion_id=abc123XYZ; src=54.12.23.45; ua="curl/7.68.0"; action=token_exchange; result=200
saml.assertion_id=abc123XYZ; src=18.204.17.92; ua="curl/7.68.0"; action=token_exchange; result=200
```
Pattern: identical assertion id used from multiple IPs within seconds.
Natalie: Confirmed KMS usage normal. Platform KMS keys show expected decrypt counts. No sign of key compromise.
Jamie: Found infra PR from `infra-service-bot` 3 days ago that granted `sts:AssumeRole` to the `legacy-integration` service account for SSO token minting. Rolling that back now and revoking the token.
Devon: Action items (assigning):
  1) Revoke all active tokens for `legacy-integration` (Jamie) — ETA 15m
  2) Roll back the permissive role change (Jamie) — ETA 30m
  3) Customer comms + SOC notif (Devon/Natalie) — ETA 30m
  4) Add assertion-replay detection to runbook + prod monitors (Sara) — ETA 2h
  5) Postmortem & follow-up (Natalie) — draft in 4h
I'll coordinate and update this thread with status.
ops-bot: [automated] Customer notification queued: 12 tenants flagged. Email templates staged.
Natalie: Starting postmortem draft. Question for the group: do we want to rotate any platform KMS keys? My read — no immediate need, but rotate service account creds and enforce scoped, short-lived tokens for `legacy-integration`.
Sara: Agreed. Also propose we add nonce/non-replay validation in the SSO middleware (drop duplicate assertion IDs within a 5m sliding window) and add alerting on assertion reuse rate >5/min.
Jamie: Patching SSO connector now — pushing a hotfix to drop duplicate assertion IDs and block token exchange when reuse detected. Will monitor metrics after merge.
Devon: If replay counts don't drop within 30m, escalate to IdP vendor (Okta) and consider emergency cert reissue. Created follow-up ticket INFSEC-1429.
Leo: :thumbsup: Dashboards show a clear decline in exchange events after throttles applied. I'll keep an eye on MFA push volume and customer feedback.
Sara: After rollback & fixes, plan to run a targeted audit for other service accounts with broad assume-role perms. Will post list here.
Natalie: Postmortem draft link: https://redwood-internal/postmortems/INFSEC-1429 (working). Will include KMS findings and timeline.
Devon: Thanks everyone — great quick work. We'll keep the thread updated. If anyone sees a reappearance, ping me and escalate immediately.
